normalized_shared_proposition: The learned whole card dain has a proposed through-cloth reading.
reason: Both sources retain that complete directional/medium phrase for the same written whole. German durch Tuch versus durch ein Tuch is an article-level paraphrase here. Neither source states exactly one cloth, a special cloth identity, a conflicting domain, or a universal all-occurrences quantifier. The quantity-family exception changes explanatory/evidential role, not this shared proposed lexical relation.
disagreement_with_MD: Different source histories alone do not establish non-equivalence. The current scopes are source-bound working hypotheses, and both original cases must remain visible; display grouping does not assert identical evidence or a shared confirmed language model.
preserve: Both source cases and their limits, including weak two-example support inV44.
Indivisible learned card OR homograph exception alternative inV44.
No assertion that every dain occurrence means through cloth.
No export of d/ain components; no noun-only TUCH equivalence.
Existing BT:DAIN:full-proposition-relation to EINLAGE remains related_not_equivalent and must not become transitive equivalence.

inherited_status_not_adopted.text: Status: **selected working grammar, not deciphered plaintext**

evidence.quote:
The ten most frequent remaining whole cards were reviewed separately. Three
keep their useful learned values (`chety|chty=zerkleinern`, `dain=durch Tuch`,
`dl=Badezusatz`). Seven now use the existing component inventory:
evidence.source_section: Seven recurrent whole cards become compositional

evidence.quote:
`dain = durch ein Tuch` ist der wichtigste Gegenfall. Ich würde ihn vorläufig
als unteilbare Karte oder homographe Ausnahme behandeln, nicht die starke
Mengenfamilie wegen eines schwachen Zweierbelegs aufgeben.
